message.content: In Christianity, the central figure is Jesus Christ, who is regarded as the Son of God and the Savior of humanity. While Jesus is not typically referred to as a “prophet” in the same way that Old Testament figures such as Isaiah or Jeremiah are, many Christians view Him as the ultimate fulfillment of prophetic promises made throughout the Hebrew Scriptures. Other prophets—such as Moses, Isaiah, Jeremiah, and John the Baptist—are also highly respected within Christian tradition for their roles in revealing God's will and preparing the way for Jesus. The importance of each prophet can vary depending on theological perspective and denominational emphasis.
